Forward Deployed Engineer

LocationFlexible (with frequent on-site work at financial institutions) TypeFull-time
Apply

Ethereum Institutional is a nonprofit focused on accelerating institutional adoption of Ethereum. We work directly with financial institutions, market infrastructure providers, and ecosystem builders to help design and deploy Ethereum-based solutions.

We are seeking a Forward Deployed Engineer who can sit in the room with senior stakeholders at banks, asset managers, custodians, and other financial institutions, and work hands-on on problem framing, technical scoping, and early solution design. This role sits at the intersection of engineering, product, and client advisory, and is ideal for a technically strong engineer who can operate comfortably in institutional environments.

Key Responsibilities

  • Join client-facing sessions with financial institutions to understand their workflows, systems, and constraints, and translate them into concrete Ethereum-based solution opportunities.
  • Lead technical discovery and scoping: map integration points, identify relevant infrastructure (custody, nodes, L2s, tokenization stacks), and outline technical architectures.
  • Build proofs-of-concept, reference implementations, and technical demos that help institutions understand how Ethereum can support tokenization, stablecoins, onchain finance, and related use cases.
  • Work closely with institutional stakeholders (IT, architecture, risk, compliance, and product teams) to address practical integration questions and constraints.
  • Produce clear technical documentation, diagrams, and implementation notes that can be handed off to internal teams or external vendors.
  • Collaborate with ecosystem teams (infra providers, protocol teams, tooling vendors) to align institutional needs with available technology.
  • Provide feedback into our content, standards, and best-practice work based on real-world engagements.

Candidate Profile

  • 5–10+ years of hands-on software engineering experience (e.g., backend, infrastructure, or full-stack) working with production systems.
  • Strong familiarity with Ethereum: smart contracts, tooling, basic protocol-level concepts, and at least one major language (e.g., Solidity, TypeScript, Python, or Go).
  • Experience integrating with financial or fintech systems (APIs, messaging, core banking, trading or settlement infrastructure, custody, etc.), or close collaboration with such teams.
  • Ability to communicate clearly with both technical and non-technical stakeholders, including senior institutional decision-makers.
  • Comfortable operating in client environments: asking structured questions, framing problems, and steering discussions toward concrete technical options.
  • Pragmatic and solution-oriented mindset, with the ability to move from “whiteboard” to working prototypes.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Prior experience in a forward-deployed / solutions engineering / field engineering / technical consultant role.
  • Experience with institutional digital-asset projects (tokenization, custody, settlement, stablecoins, or related initiatives).
  • Familiarity with cloud, security, and compliance considerations typical for financial institutions.
  • Experience creating internal tools, reference architectures, or reusable components that accelerate future engagements.

What We Offer

  • The opportunity to work directly with leading financial institutions on their earliest Ethereum initiatives.
  • A role with high visibility into both the institutional and Ethereum ecosystem sides.
  • Flexible, mission-driven environment with scope to shape best practices and standards.
  • Competitive compensation aligned with experience.
Apply

Job Summary:


We are looking for a friendly, organized, and professional Front Office Administrator to serve as the first point of contact for visitors, clients, and employees. This role is responsible for managing front desk operations, supporting administrative functions, and helping create a welcoming, efficient, and well-organized workplace environment. The successful candidate will play a key role in ensuring smooth day-to-day office operations while delivering an excellent employee and visitor experience.

What you will be responsible for:

  • Welcome and assist visitors, clients, and employees in a courteous, professional, and service-oriented manner.
  • Manage visitor & employee registration processes, including issuing visitor badges, access cards, or QR codes, and coordinating with building security to ensure compliance with security protocols.
  • Coordinate meeting room bookings and maintain office calendars, ensuring efficient use of shared spaces and adherence to workplace and meeting room etiquette.
  • Support corporate travel booking activities, including flight, hotel, and ground transportation arrangements, ensuring compliance with company policy and budget requirements.
  • Manage incoming and outgoing mail, courier services, deliveries, and distribution of correspondence.
  • Monitor office supplies and pantry inventory, coordinating replenishment as required to support daily operations.
  • Assist in organizing company events and employee engagement activities, including birthday celebrations, team-building events, and internal gatherings.
  • Support internal communications by coordinating announcements, newsletters, and other employee updates.
  • Maintain a clean, organized, and professional reception area, meeting rooms, and common office spaces.
  • Liaise with vendors, service providers, and building management to ensure office facilities and services are maintained effectively.
  • Support workplace initiatives that enhance employee experience and contribute to a positive office culture.
  • Perform other administrative and ad hoc duties as assigned by management.

About the Role

Union is taking its platform into deep, long-running partnerships with the largest infrastructure providers in the industry, including AWS, OpenAI, GCP, Azure, NeoClouds, and Apple. Each one is a multi-quarter engineering effort, not a business development handshake. It means porting our product to run natively on the partner's stack, then figuring out how that product gets packaged and installed across the wide range of enterprise environments their customers run.

We're hiring an Engineering Manager to run the two teams that make this possible.

Partner Engineering carries each hyperscaler and OEM relationship (AWS, OpenAI, GCP, Azure, NeoClouds, Apple, and others) through a roughly nine-month integration cycle, porting Union's product onto the partner's infrastructure and control planes.

Deployment Engineering turns what comes out of those integrations into a maintained, repeatable install surface: containers, Helm charts, Terraform modules, marketplace listings, and BYOC or self-managed variants. The goal is that the product installs correctly across enterprise environments without bespoke one-off engineering per customer.

We don't ship an integration and move on. We stay close to what each partnership actually requires in production, and translate real integration and install problems into reusable patterns, automation, and playbooks that make the next partnership smoother than the last.

  • Own planning and delivery across partner integrations and deployment formats.

Build a Safer World.

TRM Labs provides AI-powered intelligence solutions that help public and private sector agencies investigate and disrupt crime. TRM's platforms enable investigators to trace illicit activity, build cases, and construct operating pictures of threat networks. Leading agencies and businesses worldwide rely on TRM to make the world safer and more secure.


As Assistant General Counsel, Commercial and GTM Partnerships you’ll be a key leader of TRM’s Legal team, which The Financial Times recently named one of the “Most Innovative In-House Legal Teams in North America.” You’ll partner closely with Go‑To‑Market, Product, Engineering, Operations, and leadership. And you will own complex commercial negotiations; guide product development (including AI‑driven features and data usage); and design scalable, AI‑assisted legal workflows that let the team focus on the hardest problems instead of repetitive tasks.

Success in this role looks like a Legal function that is fast, trusted, and deeply embedded in the business: deals close on time, product teams ship with clear guardrails, and routine work runs through well‑designed, measurable processes rather than one‑off fire drills.

AI Fluency is a Core Requirement at TRM-Legal

This role operates in an AI-native legal function. You are expected to actively use generative AI tools (e.g., Claude, ChatGPT, contract CLM/AI platforms) in your daily workflow—for drafting, contract analysis, legal research, and process design. “Willingness to learn” is not enough: we look for demonstrated fluency, sound judgment about when to deploy AI vs. when to escalate to a human, and a track record of building or improving AI-assisted workflows.

The impact you’ll have here

  • Manage and develop a team of commercial attorneys and legal professionals — including hiring, mentoring, setting priorities, and creating a culture of high performance and continuous improvement. Build and scale the commercial legal team in line with company growth, including hiring, structuring coverage, and developing team members at all levels

  • Draft, review, and negotiate complex commercial agreements, with a primary focus on GTM and partnership deals across enterprise and government customers — including master subscription agreements, data and content licenses, strategic partnerships, and public sector contracts. Oversee counterparty and vendor due diligence as part of the commercial intake and contracting process

  • Navigate cross-border commercial complexity, including GDPR, UK data protection law, EU regulatory frameworks, and APAC-specific requirements, in support of a globally distributed deal pipeline across the Americas, EMEA, and Asia

  • Partner closely with Sales, Partnerships, Product, and Engineering leadership to support deal velocity and provide practical, business-oriented legal guidance. Operate as a key decision-maker on commercial legal risk, with direct escalation path to the GC/CLO on high-stakes matters

  • Support team members’ professional growth through regular feedback, stretch assignments, and opportunities to take ownership of meaningful work.

  • With legal team colleagues, navigate global regulatory complexity across privacy, AI regulation, law enforcement data access, sanctions/AML, and public procurement — translating developments into clear requirements for cross-functional teams.

  • Build and maintain commercial legal infrastructure, including contract templates, fallback playbooks, and CLM workflows, and ensure they are actually used.

  • Lead AI-enabled legal operations — designing and iterating AI-assisted workflows that improve efficiency and free attorneys to focus on judgment-intensive work.

  • Identify, frame, and escalate legal and business risks clearly, helping stakeholders make informed decisions in ambiguous situations.

  • Stay current on legal developments affecting AI technologies, data products, and the financial crime compliance space.

What we’re looking for

  • Experience. 10+ years of legal experience with a strong mix of top‑tier law firm and in‑house work, ideally in SaaS, fintech, cybersecurity, or crypto/Web3.

  • Commercial & product depth. Significant experience negotiating complex B2B technology agreements and providing hands‑on product counseling (ideally in data‑ and analytics‑heavy products).

  • AI, data, and privacy literacy. Comfort advising on AI and data issues (e.g., data sources and permissions, privacy and security obligations, AI regulatory frameworks, content and IP questions), with the ability to quickly get smart on new regimes.

  • Government and institutional customers (plus). Familiarity with public sector procurement, bank/vendor risk processes, or working with law enforcement or financial institutions is a strong plus.

  • Builder mindset. You think in systems, workflows, and SLAs, and you enjoy turning ad hoc processes into scalable, documented ones—often with the help of CLM, Salesforce, and generative AI tools.

  • AI‑native working style. Demonstrated comfort using AI tools for drafting, summarization, research, and workflow design, as well as good judgment about when a matter should bypass AI and go straight to a human.

  • Communication and judgment. Excellent drafting and negotiation skills, with the ability to explain complex issues clearly to non‑lawyers and to calibrate advice for executives, GTM leaders, and technical teams.

  • High ownership, low ego. Ability to manage a high volume of matters, balance competing priorities, and move quickly while maintaining high standards—all while being a collaborative, humble teammate.

  • Qualifications. J.D. (or international equivalent) and active bar membership in good standing in at least one U.S. jurisdiction (or ability to register in‑house where required).

 

Application Instructions

If you’re interested in joining TRM, we encourage you to apply directly. Every application is reviewed by our Talent team.

Before applying, review the job description carefully and highlight the experience and impact that best demonstrate the required qualifications. Please also provide thoughtful and accurate answers to the application questions, as these will be used to evaluate your qualifications for the role.

If you send your resume directly to someone at TRM, we can’t guarantee it will reach the appropriate hiring team. Applying directly is the best way to ensure you’re considered.

What to Expect From Our Interview Process

Our process is designed to understand how you think, solve problems, and deliver impact, while giving you the opportunity to evaluate TRM. Most interview processes include a case study, AI skills assessment, and Leadership Principles interview.

  • Recruiter Intro: Explore your experience, motivations, and alignment with the role.

  • Hiring Manager: Dive deeper into your relevant experience, skills, and impact.

  • First Round: Typically 1–2 interviews focused on the skills most critical to the role.

  • Final Round: Typically 3–5 interviews to go deeper on your craft, problem-solving, and alignment with TRM.

  • References: We’ll speak with former colleagues who can provide perspective on your work and impact.

  • Offer: If it’s a mutual fit, your recruiter will walk you through your offer and answer your questions.

  • Welcome to TRM: Once you sign, we’ll get you ready for your first day and onboarding.

Your recruiter will share your specific interview plan and preparation guidance along the way.

Learn more about interviewing at TRM

Life at TRM

We are building a safer world. That promise shows up in how we work every day.

TRM moves quickly. We are a high velocity, high ownership team that expects clarity, follow-through, and impact. People who thrive here are energized by hard problems, experimentation, and continuous feedback. If something takes months elsewhere, it will ship here in days.

Our work sits at the intersection of AI, national security, and fighting crime. The problems are complex, the stakes are real, and the environment evolves quickly. The pace and intensity of the work reflect the importance of the mission. As a result, the way we operate requires a high level of ownership, adaptability, collaboration, and creative problem-solving.

At TRM, you should expect:

  • Priorities and targets to change quickly as we experiment and iterate

  • Work that often requires operating with a high degree of ambiguity

  • A high level of personal ownership and accountability

  • Close collaboration across teams and functions

  • Frequent, high-touch communication

  • Creative problem solving and out-of-the-box thinking

  • A pace that rewards urgency, adaptability, and outcomes

This environment is energizing for people who enjoy building, solving hard problems, and making progress in situations that are not always fully defined. It also requires comfort navigating ambiguity, adjusting course as new information emerges, and maintaining focus and positivity in a fast-moving and intense environment.

We also recognize that this style of operating is not for everyone. If you are primarily optimizing for predictability or a consistently balanced workload, we encourage you to use the interview process to pressure test whether this environment is truly the right fit. We want teammates who thrive here, not just survive here.

At the same time, many people find this work deeply rewarding. If you are excited by meaningful problems, motivated by ambitious goals, and energized by working alongside mission-driven colleagues, there is a good chance you will find TRM to be an exceptional place to grow and contribute. Learn more: Interviewing at TRM: How We Hire and What Success Looks Like

 

AI Fluency at TRM

AI fluency is a baseline expectation at TRM.

We believe AI meaningfully changes how top performers operate. We expect every team member to use AI to accelerate and reimagine their craft, not just automate surface tasks.

At TRM, AI fluency means you are among the top 10 percent of operators in your function in how you apply AI to:

  • Accelerate repeatable workflows

  • Structure and solve problems

  • Improve output quality

  • Increase speed and leverage

You will be evaluated on applied AI fluency during the interview process.

Leadership Principles

We hire and grow against three leadership principles. They’re the standards for how we operate, treat each other, and make decisions.

  • Impact-Oriented Trailblazer: We put customers first and move with speed, focus, and adaptability. We treat every plan like an experiment – test, ship, measure, and iterate quickly.

  • Master Craftsperson: We care deeply about our craft. We balance speed with high standards, own outcomes end‑to‑end, and invest in getting better everyday.

  • Inspiring Colleague: We add clarity and energy, not noise. We bring humility, candor, and a one‑team mindset — giving and receiving feedback to make the team stronger.

Join our Mission

At TRM we care deeply about our craft. We are looking for individuals who want their work to matter, who experiment with speed and rigor, and who take pride in building a safer world for billions of people. If you’re excited by TRM’s mission but don’t check every box, we encourage you to apply — we hire for slope, judgment, and the will to learn fast.

Rain is the global stablecoin payments platform for enterprises, neobanks, platforms, developers, and AI agents. Our technology allows partners to move, store, and use stablecoins instantly and compliantly through global payment cards, rewards, on/offramps, wallets, and cross-border rails. As both a Visa and Mastercard Principal Member, Rain issues cards that work at more than 175 million merchant locations in over 220 countries and territories. Built natively for stablecoins and trusted by more than 100 organizations worldwide, Rain delivers secure, scalable infrastructure that makes money move freely and instantly around the world.

You will have the opportunity to deliver massive impact at a hypergrowth company backed by some of the top investors in fintech, crypto, and SaaS. In January 2026, we closed a $250M Series C led by ICONIQ, valuing Rain at $1.95B, with Sapphire Ventures, Dragonfly, Bessemer Venture Partners, Galaxy Ventures, FirstMark, Lightspeed, Norwest, and Endeavor Catalyst also participating. If you're curious, bold, and excited to help shape a borderless financial future, we'd love to talk.

 

Our Ethos

We believe in an open and flat structure. You will be able to grow into the role that most aligns with your goals. Our team members at all levels have the freedom to explore ideas and impact the roadmap and vision of our company.

About the Team

We are hiring a Head of Engineering to own the craft, quality, and technical direction of a roughly 50-person engineering organization. This is deliberately not a role about growing headcount to 150. It is a role about making a small, senior team produce output that looks like a much larger one — by raising the engineering bar, tightening the systems that move real money, and being genuinely in the code and the architecture rather than adjacent to it.

You will lead through a mix of direct reports and a small group of engineering managers and tech leads, partnering closely with Product, Risk, and Compliance. You will spend your time on design reviews, incident retros, hiring, and the handful of technical bets that determine whether we can support the next order of magnitude of transaction volume.

If your ideal week is entirely calendar blocks and roadmap decks, this is not the right role. If your ideal week includes a hard design debate, a code review that changes someone's mind, and a coaching conversation that raises a manager's ceiling, keep reading.

What you’ll do

  • Own engineering strategy and architecture across card issuing, wallets, ledger, money movement, onchain settlement, and integrations with card networks and banking partners — including the multi-year technical roadmap that gets us there.

  • Set and own Rain's engineering quality bar across system design, code review, testing, observability, documentation, and technical decision-making, ensuring correctness is treated as critical for systems that move customer funds.

  • Go deep where the risk is. You won't own day-to-day code, but you will review critical designs, weigh in on the highest-consequence architecture and build-vs.-buy decisions, and be technical enough that no one can hand you a bad design and have it pass.

  • Drive reliability, scalability, and operational excellence by establishing SLOs, improving incident response, capacity planning for 10x growth, and designing resilient systems with graceful degradation, idempotency, and replay capabilities.

  • Build security, compliance, and correctness into the platform by design, partnering closely with Risk, Compliance, and Security to meet PCI, SOC 2, fraud-control, regulatory, and blockchain infrastructure requirements.

  • Increase engineering velocity without sacrificing quality through improvements to CI/CD, developer tooling, local environments, technical debt management, and architecture that enables teams to ship safely and independently.

  • Build and develop a high-performing engineering organization by hiring and coaching engineering managers and technical leads, establishing clear team ownership and boundaries, and owning headcount planning and the performance bar.

  • Operate as a member of the leadership team — translating company strategy into technical plans, partnering across Product, Design, Risk, Compliance, and GTM, and representing engineering to the board, banking and network partners, and customers.

You are likely to succeed if you have:

  • 15+ years building production software, including 8+ years leading engineers and meaningful time leading managers.

  • Current technical credibility. You have written or reviewed meaningful production code recently enough that an architecture review is a place you add value, not a place you nod along.

  • Deep experience with distributed backend systems at scale: data modeling, consistency and idempotency, queues and event-driven design, and the operational reality of running all of it.

  • A track record of raising an engineering bar. You can point to specific practices you introduced and the measurable change in quality, velocity, or reliability that followed.

  • Real reliability ownership — you have carried a pager, run incident command during a serious outage, and built the follow-through that kept it from recurring.

  • Experience in payments, fintech, banking infrastructure, or another domain where money, ledgers, or regulatory obligations made correctness non-negotiable.

  • You have hired and developed engineering managers, not only engineers. There are leaders you grew who would come work for you again.

  • Clear written communication. You can make a complex technical tradeoff legible to a CEO, a compliance officer, and a partner's engineering team in the same week.

  • Executive range. You are as comfortable in a board or partner conversation as you are in a design review, and you can hold a technical position under commercial pressure.

  • Comfort with ambiguity and speed. You would rather ship something correct this quarter than design something perfect for next year.

Bonus attributes:

  • Hands-on experience with card issuing, processing, or the Visa and Mastercard network stack.

  • Working knowledge of stablecoins, onchain settlement, custody and key management, or EVM and Solana infrastructure.

  • Experience operating under SOC 2, PCI DSS, or bank and program-manager oversight.

  • Experience leading distributed or multi-region teams.

Unlimited time off 🌴 Unlimited vacation can be daunting, so we require Rainmakers to take 10 days minimum for themselves.

Flexible working ☕ We support a flexible workplace – work from home, come into an office, or both. We want everyone to work in an environment where they're their most confident and productive selves. New Rainmakers receive a stipend to set up a comfortable home workspace.

Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $200B in annualized spend flows in and out of 70,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books.

The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving.

We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome.

The median Ramp customer saves 5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year – far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same.

If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it.

Ramp is hiring Executive Assistants to partner with senior leaders across the company. Our EAs play a critical role in helping executives operate at their best—creating focus, removing friction, anticipating needs, and ensuring important work moves forward.

For us, being AI-first is not about replacing human judgement. It is about combining human expertise, creativity and accountability with technology that helps us do our best work and accelerate our growth. In the end, that's what we're hiring for: human insight, supercharged by AI.

We are seeking a seasoned Senior Risk Manager with 10+ years of risk management experience at a CFTC-registered Derivatives Clearing Organization (DCO) to join our risk function. This individual will play a critical role in safeguarding the integrity of our clearinghouse by leading the design, calibration, and ongoing oversight of margin models, stress testing frameworks, and broader market risk methodologies. The successful candidate will work cross-functionally with clearing operations, technology, compliance, and senior leadership to ensure that the DCO’s risk management framework meets the highest regulatory and industry standards. Prior experience at a Futures Commission Merchant (FCM) is strongly preferred and will bring valuable perspective on the participant side of cleared markets.

  • Margin Modeling & Methodology

    • Ongoing performance monitoring of initial and variation margin models across cleared products, including futures, options, and swaps.

    • Lead periodic recalibration of margin parameters (lookback windows, volatility scaling, anti-procyclicality measures, liquidity add-ons, concentration charges) and document changes in accordance with the DCO’s model governance framework.

    • Evaluate and enhance portfolio-based margining methodologies (e.g., SPAN-style, VaR/Expected Shortfall, filtered historical simulation) for accuracy, defensibility, and regulatory compliance.

    • Conduct back-testing, sensitivity analysis, and model performance reviews; clearly articulate findings to internal stakeholders, the Risk Committee, and regulators.

    • Design, execute, and continuously refine the DCO’s stress testing program, including historical, hypothetical, and reverse stress scenarios.

    • Monitor market risk exposures of clearing members and the clearinghouse as a whole, including concentration, wrong-way risk, liquidity risk, and tail-risk exposures.

    • Assess the adequacy of the default waterfall, guaranty fund sizing, and skin-in-the-game contributions in light of evolving market conditions.

    • Produce daily, weekly, and monthly risk reporting to senior management, the Risk Committee, and external regulators.

    • Ensure ongoing compliance with CFTC Part 39 DCO Core Principles, including those governing financial resources, margin, risk management, default procedures, and system safeguards.

    • Serve as a liaison to the CFTC and other regulators during examinations, rule certifications, and ad hoc inquiries.

    • Maintain robust model risk management documentation aligned with industry standards and the DCO’s internal governance policies.

    • Support the Chief Risk Officer in Risk Committee preparation, member due diligence, and the evaluation of new products and clearing services.

    • Conduct financial and operational risk reviews of clearing members, including assessment of capital adequacy, liquidity, and risk management practices.

    • Monitor intraday and end-of-day exposures, margin calls, and collateral sufficiency; escalate emerging risks to the CRO and senior leadership.

    • Partner with operations and technology to enhance real-time risk monitoring tools and dashboards.

What you bring

  • Minimum of 10 years of risk management experience at a CFTC-registered DCO, with direct ownership of margin and/or stress testing methodologies.

  • Deep, practical knowledge of CFTC regulations, particularly Part 39 DCO Core Principles, and familiarity with adjacent rules under Parts 1, 22, and 190.

  • Demonstrated expertise in market risk concepts: VaR, Expected Shortfall, scenario analysis, volatility modeling, and portfolio risk aggregation across futures and options.

  • Foundation in margin model design and validation (SPAN, SPAN 2, historical simulation, parametric, or Monte Carlo-based approaches).

  • Hands-on experience designing and executing stress testing programs that meet DCO regulatory expectations (liquidity stress, default management drills).

  • Bachelor’s degree required in a quantitative discipline (Finance, Economics, Mathematics, Statistics, Engineering, or related field); advanced degree (Master’s) preferred.

  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with proven ability to present complex risk concepts to executives, board members, and regulators.

  • Sound judgment under pressure, with the ability to make defensible risk decisions in volatile markets.

  • Intellectual rigor and attention to detail in model design, validation, and documentation.

  • Collaborative orientation across risk, operations, technology, compliance, and legal functions.

  • Comfort engaging directly with regulators, clearing members, and senior internal stakeholders.

Nice to haves

  • Prior experience at a Futures Commission Merchant (FCM), including familiarity with customer segregation requirements, house vs. customer margining, and FCM risk management practices.

  • Experience with cleared derivatives across multiple asset classes (digital assets, interest rates, energy, agricultural, metals, equity indices, FX).

  • Working knowledge of default management processes, including auction protocols, hedging, and porting of customer positions.

  • Experience supporting regulatory examinations, rule filings, or new product self-certifications under CFTC Part 40.

About MoonPay Enterprise

MoonPay Enterprise is one of the more operationally complex products in the stablecoin space: multiple banking providers, multiple payment rails, a growing partner base across two product lines (Orchestration and Issuance), and an active compliance surface across each. MoonPay Enterprise runs B2B, B2B2B, and B2B2C models. Partners integrate our API. Their customers become direct customers of MoonPay Enterprise for compliance purposes.

KYB is the front door. Every partner is a business. Every business customer of every partner clears KYB before a single transaction moves. Today the flow is part automated registry verification, part manual review, with different rules for the US and the rest of the world, and turnaround measured in days. That does not scale to where MoonPay Enterprise is going. KYB has to become a product: measurable, fast, API-first, defensible in front of regulators and banking partners. This is a principal seat. You set the multi-year direction for how businesses enter MoonPay Enterprise, and you own the outcome.

What You'll Own

KYB product strategy & roadmap

  • Business onboarding end-to-end, across every model MoonPay Enterprise runs: partners onboarding onto MoonPay Enterprise, businesses onboarding directly, and business customers onboarding through partners.

  • Platform altitude. KYB decisions ripple into KYC, Travel Rule capture, banking-provider onboarding, and Issuance partner diligence. Connect the surfaces; don't optimise one in isolation.

  • MoonPay Enterprise runs three KYC delivery models (reliance, outsourcing, hosted). KYB coverage is uneven across them. You decide where it expands and in what order.

  • Genuine product depth on MoonPay Enterprise is non-negotiable. Within weeks you talk fluently about KYB outcomes, UBO requirements, virtual account structures, and API behaviour. From being hands-on, not from documentation.

Onboarding funnel & conversion

  • The KYB funnel is yours: pass rate, time-to-verified against a 48-72h target, manual review rate, drop-off per step.

  • Instrument what isn't instrumented. Make approval speed and rejection quality measurable. Then move both.

  • Fix rejection UX. Today a declined business often gets a status without a reason, and the partner escalates to support to find out what is missing. Rejection reasons, retry semantics, and resubmission flows become API surface partners build on.

KYB API & partner experience

  • The KYB API surface: statuses, webhooks, document submission, and the edge cases that make business onboarding hard (sole proprietors, corporate shareholders, one person who is UBO, Director, and Representative at once).

  • Partners integrate KYB in weeks and self-serve their onboarding questions. Every "what is missing for this customer" escalation is a product gap. Close it.

Compliance as product

  • Turn compliance-approved onboarding matrices into product logic. US and non-US differ: control prong versus directors, when ownership documents are required, self-certification options. Partners should never need to read a matrix.

  • EDD triggers, high-risk classification, prohibited industries, Travel Rule capture: you decide how they show up in the product.

  • Compliance is your sparring partner, not a ticket queue. You shape how policy becomes product. They own the policy.

Vendor & provider orchestration

  • The verification stack (SumSub today) and the build-versus-buy calls around it.

  • Cost per verification, automation rate, vendor performance. Know when a second provider, a waterfall, or in-house tooling earns its place.

  • Push automation. Decide where AI-assisted review with a human in the loop replaces manual queues, and prove it does not raise risk.

  • Every new banking provider brings its own onboarding requirements. Keep KYB compatible with every rail without collecting everything from everyone.

Who You Are

  • A principal-level PM with real KYB or KYC depth. You have owned onboarding, identity, verification, or risk as a platform, not a feature.

  • High agency. You do not wait for a mandate, a brief, or perfect data. You find the problem, claim it, and fix it.

  • Full autonomy, zero to one. Hand you an unowned surface and you take it from first principles to shipped. No handover document, no waiting for direction.

  • AI-fluent by default. AI tools are your daily instruments for analysis, prototyping, and drafting. You run your own queries; analysis is not something you request from another team.

  • Compliance is a design constraint, not a blocker. You read a requirements matrix and see API design, funnel steps, and copy.

  • You know your funnel cold: pass rate, time-to-verified, manual review rate, cost per verification.

  • At home in API-first B2B. Your users are partner engineers and the businesses behind them, not consumers.

  • You have run verification vendors (SumSub, Persona, or equivalents) and know when to switch, stack, or build.

  • A multiplier for the product team around you. You raise the bar for how compliance-heavy product work gets scoped, specced, and shipped.

  • Bias to action. Reactive stewardship of an existing flow is not what we are hiring for.

About Ramp

Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $200B in annualized spend flows in and out of 70,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books.

The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving.

We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome.

The median Ramp customer saves 5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year – far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same.

If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it.

About the Role

At Ramp, people are the single biggest lever on our trajectory, and the bar for who joins this team gets higher every quarter, not lower. We are hiring our first dedicated Recruiter for GTM Expansion, based in London: someone who can map a market, identify the operators who will outperform their peers and run a full-cycle process that wins them.

The UK is the immediate mandate. You will partner with local and US-based leaders to turn an ambitious growth plan into a real commercial team, from first conversation through offer close. You will also help us build the recruiting approach, market knowledge and candidate networks that support Ramp's expansion into new GTM markets over time.

The recruiters who do this best combine craft on the front end, research, identification and calibration, with execution on the back end, closing, candidate experience and pipeline discipline. We are looking for both.

What You'll Do

• Own full-cycle recruiting for priority GTM Expansion hiring, starting with UK roles across Sales, Solutions Consulting, Partnerships and Customer Success.

• Build a sharp point of view on the UK market and future expansion markets: the companies producing strong talent, the people who outperform their peers and the communities that matter.

• Use research, data and AI as part of your everyday craft to identify and qualify exceptional candidates. We expect a written market point of view, not just a slate of profiles.

• Run thoughtful, personalised outreach grounded in the candidate's actual background, commercial motion or recent work. We care more about quality, replies and conversion than send volume.

• Partner with GTM leaders to turn ambitious hiring plans into a clear profile, credible process and realistic compensation strategy. Surface hard market truth early and push back constructively when needed.

• Own the candidate experience from first conversation through offer close: fast follow-up, clear communication, strong process discipline and a tailored closing plan for the candidates we most want.

• Build real presence for Ramp in London through the right relationships, referrals and targeted community activity. The point is pipeline and credibility, not events for their own sake.

• Work tightly with the wider GTM Recruiting team on calibration, sourcing support, insight and operating rhythm, while bringing strong local judgment.

• Help improve how Ramp recruits for expansion by capturing what works in the UK and applying it thoughtfully as we enter new markets.

What You Need

• 5+ years of full-cycle GTM or Sales recruiting experience, ideally in a high-growth technology company where quality and pace both mattered.

• Strong knowledge of the UK technology talent market and a credible local network, or clear evidence that you can build one quickly.

• A track record of finding and closing exceptional people, not simply running inherited processes. You can point to candidates you identified who became strong hires.

• Excellent sourcing and research instincts. You can explain why someone is genuinely differentiated, not only that they have the right title at the right company.

• Experience hiring across several GTM functions, such as AEs, Sales Leadership, Solutions Consulting, Partnerships, Customer Success or RevOps.

• Strong candidate-closing judgment. You listen closely, understand what each candidate is weighing and can build conviction against serious alternatives.

• The confidence to influence senior leaders, challenge a mis-scoped search and make a hiring process better without creating unnecessary friction.

• Comfort using data to understand funnel health, diagnose problems and hold an honest conversation about what needs to change.

• High ownership. You book the next step while you have the candidate, chase what is stuck and do not wait for a detailed brief to get useful work moving.

• Specific, sharp written communication. Your outreach and candidate updates should never feel template-driven.

Nice to Have

• Experience recruiting for a fintech, SaaS, infrastructure or similarly complex B2B product.

• Experience joining a company as the first recruiter in a new geography, or helping to scale an international business.

• Experience building an AI-augmented recruiting research workflow.

Why this Role

You will have unusual ownership over one of Ramp's most important growth priorities, with the support of an established Talent team rather than the isolation of a one-person recruiting function. The work is practical and high impact: build the UK commercial team, help leaders make better hiring decisions and raise the bar for how Ramp recruits as it enters new markets.

About the Job

zerohash is hiring a VP of Ecosystem and Product Partnerships to own the company's point of view on where onchain infrastructure is going, and to turn that view into the partnerships that put zerohash at the center of it. Reporting directly to the Chief Business Officer, this role owns the full arc of ecosystem development: forming the thesis, sourcing and negotiating the partnerships that follow from it, and driving them through product and engineering to launch.

This is a role for someone who is genuinely fluent in both rooms. You should be able to sit with a protocol founder or a foundation's leadership and debate token design, sequencer economics, or bridging risk on the merits, then sit with the leadership of a global bank or exchange and explain why any of it matters to their business, in their language. zerohash's partners include Morgan Stanley, Interactive Brokers, Stripe, Franklin Templeton, BlackRock, and Worldpay. The person in this seat represents zerohash at that altitude and is credible there on day one.

Most of the counterparties are protocol-side: chains, foundations, token issuers, and infrastructure providers. What makes this hire different from a conventional partnerships leader is the ability to translate that world for institutions, publicly and privately, with the credibility to be taken seriously by both.

Responsibilities

  • Own zerohash's ecosystem thesis: which chains, tokens, standards, and infrastructure layers matter, why, and what zerohash should build toward as a result. Defend that view with the CBO, the Executive Team, and the board.
  • Lead all sourcing, evaluation, and negotiation for new chain, token, and strategic product partnerships, from first conversation to signed agreement.
  • Structure and close complex, multi-party commercial frameworks: incentive programs, milestone structures, co-marketing commitments, and long-term strategic agreements.

About Polymarket

Polymarket is the world's largest prediction market platform. We enable individuals to express views on real-world events by trading on outcomes across politics, economics, sports, culture, and current affairs. Built as a peer-to-peer marketplace with no centralized "house," Polymarket aggregates diverse opinions into transparent, market-based probabilities that reflect collective expectations about the future.

We're growing fast, both in terms of volume ($21B traded in 2025) and adoption as an alternative news source. Our ambition is to become a ubiquitous beacon of truth in global media and we need your help adding fuel to the fire.

About the Role

The exchange is the core of what Polymarket does. Every trade, every order, every market resolution runs through the systems this team owns. As a Senior Backend Engineer on the Services team, you'll be working directly on that infrastructure, building and scaling the backend that processes real money, in real time, at meaningful volume. The work is technical, high-stakes, and unambiguous in its consequences.

This is an individual contributor role with high autonomy and high ownership. You'll work alongside a small group of senior engineers who care deeply about correctness and performance. There's no heavy process here, no committees, no long approval chains. You'll be expected to identify problems, propose solutions, and ship them. The mandate is simple: keep the exchange fast, correct, and available as Polymarket continues to scale.

If you've spent your career building systems where performance actually matters, where a bug in production has real consequences, this is the kind of problem you've been waiting to work on.

What You'll Do

  • Design and implement low-latency backend services that power Polymarket's core exchange, primarily in Go, with Python or Java where appropriate.

  • Profile and tune systems across the full stack, identifying bottlenecks in latency, throughput, and memory usage before they become production problems.

  • Build and maintain event-driven data pipelines and APIs using streaming platforms like Kafka or Pulsar, ensuring data moves reliably and quickly across the exchange.

  • Own production reliability for the systems you build, including diagnosing live incidents, writing postmortems, and shipping fixes that prevent recurrence.

  • Work directly with engineers across product, infrastructure, and data to integrate exchange services tightly with the broader platform.

  • Contribute to architectural decisions on distributed systems design, with a focus on failure modes, graceful degradation, and recovery under partial outages.

What We're Looking For

  • 4 to 7+ years of professional backend development experience, with strong proficiency in Go, Python, or Java. Go experience is a significant advantage.

  • Deep understanding of algorithms, data structures, concurrency, and memory management, with a track record of applying that knowledge to real production systems.

  • Experience building and debugging high-throughput, low-latency systems on Linux end-to-end, from design through to production operation.

  • Strong instincts for correctness, especially in systems where failures have financial consequences. You write defensively, think about edge cases early, and treat bugs in prod as a serious matter.

  • Comfortable working independently in a high-autonomy environment. You identify what needs to be done and do it without waiting to be unblocked.

  • (Plus) Experience in trading systems, high-frequency trading, gaming, telecom, or any domain where latency is a hard constraint, not a stretch goal.

  • (Plus) Production experience with Kafka, Pulsar, or similar streaming platforms at meaningful scale.

  • (Plus) Familiarity with gRPC, Protobuf, or ZeroMQ.

  • (Plus) Experience deploying and operating services in cloud environments such as AWS or GCP, using containers and modern deployment tooling.

Benefits

  • Competitive salary & equity

  • Unlimited PTO

  • Full Health, Vision, & Dental coverage

  • 401k match

  • Hardware setup: new MacBook Pro, big display, & accessories

About Ramp

Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $200B in annualized spend flows in and out of 70,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books.

The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving.

We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome.

The median Ramp customer saves 5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year – far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same.

If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it.

About Production Engineering

Production Engineering is Ramp's infrastructure ownership layer. We exist to make Ramp faster, more reliable, and more scalable — and we do that by being embedded in the problems, not adjacent to them.

A few things that define how we operate:

  • One team, one company, one objective. There is no "infra team" and "product team" — there is Ramp. We share the company's goals as our own. When a product team struggles with reliability or scalability, that is our struggle.

  • If reliability or scalability is at risk, we own it. We don't wait to be invited, and we don't ask whose code it is. If a system is slow, if it breaks, if it won't scale — that's ours to lead, regardless of where it lives in the stack.

  • We go first, and we go fast. When the path isn't obvious, we don't wait for someone else to find it. We move with urgency, propose the solution, align the stakeholders, and stay in until it's done — not until our ticket is closed.

  • We lead the way. We find the next problem before it finds us. And when we solve it, we don't just fix it for ourselves — the patterns and standards we establish become the foundation the rest of Ramp builds on. That's not a side effect of the job; it's the job.

  • We stay calibrated. Speed means nothing if we're moving in the wrong direction. We regularly stop and ask honestly whether what we're working on is still the highest-leverage thing we could be doing — the discipline that makes sure our effort compounds toward what actually matters.

You cannot build the future of finance on shaky infrastructure.

Our Teams

Production Engineering is organized into teams — but we think about teams differently. Teams are mutable. We build them around what needs to be done, not around what we need to do given the teams we already have. The structure below reflects our current priorities; it will evolve as Ramp does.

Right now, we operate across four areas:

  • Compute — the foundation everything runs on: container orchestration, networking, load balancing, edge infrastructure, and the deployment systems that get code from engineers' laptops to production reliably and at scale

  • Storage — databases, caching, object storage, and the data infrastructure that underpins everything

  • Workflows & Messaging — the systems that power Ramp's financial workflows and event-driven architecture

  • Internal Infrastructure — the platform that makes every builder at Ramp faster and more autonomous: observability, cost attribution, and CI/CD systems that give teams visibility into what they build and what it costs

What You'll Do

Production Engineers at Ramp are full software engineers who happen to specialize in infrastructure. You write production code, you own systems end-to-end, and you drive technical outcomes across the organization — not just within your team.

Day to day, you will:

  • Build and operate critical infrastructure across Ramp's compute, storage, messaging, and observability stack — owning the systems that handle real financial transactions at scale.

  • Drive architectural change — not just flag problems. When you surface a reliability or scalability issue, you own the path forward: you propose the solution, find the owners across engineering, and stay in until it's resolved.

  • Partner with product teams at the design phase — reviewing architectures, embedding golden paths, and making it easy to build correctly the first time.

  • Build Ramp's next level of scale — you'll be a hands-on contributor to the most consequential infrastructure shift happening right now: our move to a cellular architecture, enabling Ramp to scale, reach international markets, operate in highly regulated and constrained environments (e.g. FedRAMP), and deliver on enterprise-grade SLAs.

  • Enable AI-native engineering — as Ramp builds increasingly AI-powered products, PE is the team that makes sure the platform can support them. You'll proactively partner with product teams on AI infrastructure patterns, define the golden paths that turn one-off solutions into reusable foundations, and stay ahead of emerging challenges before they become blockers.

  • Build developer tooling and self-service infrastructure — so that other teams can answer their own questions (cost, performance, reliability) without involving PE.

  • Participate in on-call rotation — and more importantly, use every incident as a signal to eliminate the root cause, not just resolve the symptom.

  • Lead across the company — PE doesn't just review designs or show up when called. We proactively initiate cross-team architectural reviews, and we take full ownership of company-wide reliability and scalability initiatives: identifying the problem, proposing the solution, aligning the stakeholders, and staying in until it's done.

What We Look For

We don't hire for a checklist. We hire for the instincts that make someone exceptional on this team.

The mindset we're looking for:

  • You can't walk past something broken without wanting to fix it — and you don't stop at the workaround. You find the root cause and eliminate the class of problem.

  • You think in systems, not tasks. You understand that "fixing the bug" is step one; making it so the bug can't happen again is the job.

  • You move with urgency but without chaos. You know when to go fast and when to slow down and do it right.

  • You treat product teams as your users. You build for them, communicate with them proactively, and measure success by how much faster they can ship. But you're also an owner — when something is broken or blocking, you don't wait to be asked. We win when our customers win.

  • You leave things better than you found them. Every system you touch, every process you encounter — you move it forward. Not always dramatically, but always directionally. You picked it up in a certain state; you leave it in a better one.

  • You are equally comfortable reading a database query plan, reviewing a system design doc, writing a Terraform module, and jumping into an incident at 2am.

Experience profile:

  • 3+ years of software engineering management shipping high-quality architectures for critical systems

  • Strong software engineering fundamentals — you write clean, well-tested, production-ready code

  • Hands-on experience with distributed systems at production scale

  • Experience with at least one major cloud provider (AWS preferred)

  • Familiarity with observability practices (SLOs, error budgets, alerting, dashboards)

  • Track record of leading technical projects end-to-end, including cross-team coordination

  • Comfortable using AI tooling and coding agents as part of your everyday engineering workflow — we expect our engineers to leverage these tools to move faster and think bigger

About Matter Labs

Matter Labs builds cryptographic infrastructure for global finance. The team created ZKsync and shipped the first production zero-knowledge rollup. Today we build Prividium, an Ethereum-secured blockchain platform for banks and financial institutions that need privacy, compliance, and full control of their data. Prividium runs in production: Deutsche Bank's Project DAMA 2 is built on Prividium, which also underpins Cari Network, a tokenised-deposit network developed with five US regional banks. The platform is early. The reference deployments are real, the repeatable sales motion is still being built. This role shapes the technical side of that motion.

The role

You will be the technical partner to Matter Labs' institutional sales team. Your work turns customer requirements into credible Prividium architectures and moves opportunities from discovery through evaluation into a deployment plan the customer trusts. The role owns technical discovery, solution design, evaluations and proofs of concept, and the technical response to security and due-diligence reviews. It is a hands-on presales role at the intersection of enterprise architecture, financial markets, and zero-knowledge infrastructure.

What you'll do

  • Lead technical discovery. Map customer architecture, data privacy, identity and permissions, interoperability, performance, resilience, custody, and compliance constraints.

  • Design solutions. Translate customer workflows into target architectures for Prividium, including integration boundaries, APIs, deployment models, and the route from pilot to production.

  • Deliver demos and workshops. Build and run tailored demonstrations and technical workshops for audiences from engineering teams to senior business leaders.

  • Run evaluations. Define success criteria, scope proofs of concept, coordinate internal specialists, and keep pilots tied to a commercial decision.

  • Own technical diligence. Lead responses to RFPs, RFIs, security reviews, and architecture assessments, with support from Engineering, Security, Product, and Legal.

  • Prepare implementation. Produce solution documentation with explicit assumptions, dependencies, owners, and acceptance criteria, and hand over cleanly into delivery.

  • Feed the roadmap. Bring structured customer evidence into Product and Engineering, and separate repeatable market needs from one-off requests.

Over time, the reference architectures and playbooks you build become the foundation of the solutions-engineering function.

What we look for

Each of these is a demonstrated capability, shown through work you have done:

  • 7+ years in solutions engineering, sales engineering, enterprise architecture, or technical consulting in a customer-facing setting.

  • Working with banks, capital-markets firms, market infrastructure, payments businesses, or other regulated institutions.

  • Deep grounding in APIs, distributed systems, cloud and on-premise deployment, security, identity and access, and data privacy.

  • Leading complex technical evaluations or proofs of concept and converting them into production decisions.

  • Explaining complex systems to technical and non-technical audiences, with precise writing and disciplined expectation management.

  • Aligning sales, product, engineering, security, and customer teams without formal authority.

Nice to have

Working knowledge of Ethereum, smart contracts, tokenisation, or zero-knowledge proofs. Deep enterprise and financial-services experience can compensate for a lighter crypto background.

Work model & pay

  • Competitive base salary

  • Performance-based variable compensation and a long-term token incentive are additional. Both are paid in ZK tokens. New-hire token grants vest over four years with a one-year cliff.

  • Freedom & ownership culture: no time tracking, minimum bureaucracy-only results matter.

TRM Labs provides AI-powered intelligence solutions that help public and private sector agencies investigate and disrupt crime. At TRM, we believe the people we hire will determine how far and how fast we can go in our mission to build a safer world for billions of people. As an International Sales Recruiter, you will be responsible for owning high-priority searches across EMEA and other global markets, with a focus on Sales, Post-Sales, Compliance, Marketing, and broader business recruiting. You will partner closely with hiring managers and Talent leadership to define search strategy, map regional talent markets, engage passive candidates, and drive high-quality hiring decisions with speed and precision.

Your success will be measured by the quality, velocity, and business impact of hires across TRM’s international business functions.

The impact you will have:

  • Own full-cycle recruiting for international business roles across Sales, Post-Sales, Compliance, Marketing, and other functions.

  • Act as a strategic talent partner to hiring managers, advising on market dynamics, candidate calibration, sourcing strategy, and closing approach.

  • Build and execute targeted sourcing strategies that identify, engage, and close exceptional talent across EMEA and other global markets.

  • Develop regional talent maps across priority markets, including high-performing companies, competitor talent, referral-driven networks, and specialized candidate communities.

  • Create an exceptional candidate experience, ensuring every touchpoint reflects TRM’s talent bar, mission, and operating principles.

  • Use data, market insights, and funnel conversion metrics to diagnose search health, influence hiring teams, and refine recruiting strategy in real time.

  • Drive urgency and decision quality across searches by facilitating clear calibration, structured feedback, and timely hiring decisions.

  • Continuously improve international recruiting processes, including intake quality, scorecard alignment, sourcing strategy, debrief rigor, and offer execution.

  • Partner cross-functionally with Talent, People, Finance, Legal, and business leaders to navigate international hiring considerations and keep searches moving efficiently.

  • High ownership, persistence, and judgment in navigating ambiguous, specialized, and business-critical searches.

  • Ability to operate effectively in a remote, globally distributed environment with strong overlap across EMEA and U.S. business hours.

About the Team:

  • The estimated base salary range for this role is $153,000 - $172,000.

  • Additionally, this role may be eligible to participate in TRM’s equity plan.

  • Please note – we factor in the different costs for geographies outside the United States.

Application Instructions

If you’re interested in joining TRM, we encourage you to apply directly. Every application is reviewed by our Talent team.

Before applying, review the job description carefully and highlight the experience and impact that best demonstrate the required qualifications. Please also provide thoughtful and accurate answers to the application questions, as these will be used to evaluate your qualifications for the role.

If you send your resume directly to someone at TRM, we can’t guarantee it will reach the appropriate hiring team. Applying directly is the best way to ensure you’re considered.

What to Expect From Our Interview Process

Our process is designed to understand how you think, solve problems, and deliver impact, while giving you the opportunity to evaluate TRM. Most interview processes include a case study, AI skills assessment, and Leadership Principles interview.

  • Recruiter Intro: Explore your experience, motivations, and alignment with the role.

  • Hiring Manager: Dive deeper into your relevant experience, skills, and impact.

  • First Round: Typically 1–2 interviews focused on the skills most critical to the role.

  • Final Round: Typically 3–5 interviews to go deeper on your craft, problem-solving, and alignment with TRM.

  • References: We’ll speak with former colleagues who can provide perspective on your work and impact.

  • Offer: If it’s a mutual fit, your recruiter will walk you through your offer and answer your questions.

  • Welcome to TRM: Once you sign, we’ll get you ready for your first day and onboarding.

Your recruiter will share your specific interview plan and preparation guidance along the way.

Learn more about interviewing at TRM

Life at TRM

We are building a safer world. That promise shows up in how we work every day.

TRM moves quickly. We are a high velocity, high ownership team that expects clarity, follow-through, and impact. People who thrive here are energized by hard problems, experimentation, and continuous feedback. If something takes months elsewhere, it will ship here in days.

Our work sits at the intersection of AI, national security, and fighting crime. The problems are complex, the stakes are real, and the environment evolves quickly. The pace and intensity of the work reflect the importance of the mission. As a result, the way we operate requires a high level of ownership, adaptability, collaboration, and creative problem-solving.

At TRM, you should expect:

  • Priorities and targets to change quickly as we experiment and iterate

  • Work that often requires operating with a high degree of ambiguity

  • A high level of personal ownership and accountability

  • Close collaboration across teams and functions

  • Frequent, high-touch communication

  • Creative problem solving and out-of-the-box thinking

  • A pace that rewards urgency, adaptability, and outcomes

This environment is energizing for people who enjoy building, solving hard problems, and making progress in situations that are not always fully defined. It also requires comfort navigating ambiguity, adjusting course as new information emerges, and maintaining focus and positivity in a fast-moving and intense environment.

We also recognize that this style of operating is not for everyone. If you are primarily optimizing for predictability or a consistently balanced workload, we encourage you to use the interview process to pressure test whether this environment is truly the right fit. We want teammates who thrive here, not just survive here.

At the same time, many people find this work deeply rewarding. If you are excited by meaningful problems, motivated by ambitious goals, and energized by working alongside mission-driven colleagues, there is a good chance you will find TRM to be an exceptional place to grow and contribute. Learn more: Interviewing at TRM: How We Hire and What Success Looks Like

 

AI Fluency at TRM

What to Expect From Our Interview Process

Our process is designed to understand how you think, solve problems, and deliver impact, while giving you the opportunity to evaluate TRM. Most interview processes include a case study, AI skills assessment, and Leadership Principles interview.

  • Recruiter Intro: Explore your experience, motivations, and alignment with the role.

Life at TRM

We are building a safer world. That promise shows up in how we work every day.

TRM moves quickly. We are a high velocity, high ownership team that expects clarity, follow-through, and impact. People who thrive here are energized by hard problems, experimentation, and continuous feedback. If something takes months elsewhere, it will ship here in days.

Our work sits at the intersection of AI, national security, and fighting crime. The problems are complex, the stakes are real, and the environment evolves quickly. The pace and intensity of the work reflect the importance of the mission. As a result, the way we operate requires a high level of ownership, adaptability, collaboration, and creative problem-solving.

At TRM, you should expect:

  • Priorities and targets to change quickly as we experiment and iterate

  • Work that often requires operating with a high degree of ambiguity

  • A high level of personal ownership and accountability

  • Close collaboration across teams and functions

  • Frequent, high-touch communication

  • Creative problem solving and out-of-the-box thinking

  • A pace that rewards urgency, adaptability, and outcomes

This environment is energizing for people who enjoy building, solving hard problems, and making progress in situations that are not always fully defined. It also requires comfort navigating ambiguity, adjusting course as new information emerges, and maintaining focus and positivity in a fast-moving and intense environment.

We also recognize that this style of operating is not for everyone. If you are primarily optimizing for predictability or a consistently balanced workload, we encourage you to use the interview process to pressure test whether this environment is truly the right fit. We want teammates who thrive here, not just survive here.

At the same time, many people find this work deeply rewarding. If you are excited by meaningful problems, motivated by ambitious goals, and energized by working alongside mission-driven colleagues, there is a good chance you will find TRM to be an exceptional place to grow and contribute. AI Fluency at TRM

AI fluency is a baseline expectation at TRM.

We believe AI meaningfully changes how top performers operate. We expect every team member to use AI to accelerate and reimagine their craft, not just automate surface tasks.

At TRM, AI fluency means you are among the top 10 percent of operators in your function in how you apply AI to:

  • Accelerate repeatable workflows

  • Structure and solve problems

  • Improve output quality

  • Increase speed and leverage

  • Impact-Oriented Trailblazer: We put customers first and move with speed, focus, and adaptability. We treat every plan like an experiment – test, ship, measure, and iterate quickly.

  • Inspiring Colleague: We add clarity and energy, not noise. We bring humility, candor, and a one‑team mindset — giving and receiving feedback to make the team stronger.

Join our Mission

At TRM we care deeply about our craft. We are looking for individuals who want their work to matter, who experiment with speed and rigor, and who take pride in building a safer world for billions of people. If you’re excited by TRM’s mission but don’t check every box, we encourage you to apply — we hire for slope, judgment, and the will to learn fast.

Build a Safer World.

TRM Labs provides AI-powered intelligence solutions that help public and private sector agencies investigate and disrupt crime. TRM's platforms enable investigators to trace illicit activity, build cases, and construct operating pictures of threat networks. Leading agencies and businesses worldwide rely on TRM to make the world safer and more secure.

As the Head of Strategic Finance, you will be a senior leader shaping TRM’s trajectory during a period of rapid growth. Reporting to the VP of Finance, you will build and lead a high-performing Strategic Finance team responsible for enabling TRM’s continued success through rigorous planning, analysis, and decision-making support. You will drive our company-wide financial planning processes, partnering with executives to align resource allocation with strategic priorities. This role offers a unique opportunity to influence decisions across the entire business, from Product to Sales to G&A, and to engage closely with our Board and investors.

The impact you will have:

  • Own and lead TRM’s long-range (multi-year), annual, and quarterly planning cycles in close collaboration with executive leadership

     

  • Build and scale a high-performing Strategic Finance team that acts as a trusted thought partner to senior leaders

     

  • Develop and maintain robust financial models to support corporate strategy, scenario planning, and key investments

     

  • Establish and continuously improve processes and systems for forecasting, performance reporting, and budget management

     

  • Define, track, and analyze key business metrics; deliver insights that influence strategic decisions and improve financial outcomes

     

  • Play a critical role in M&A, capital markets, and investor relations

 
 

What we’re looking for:

  • 8–10+ years of experience across investment banking, private equity, consulting, venture capital, or strategic finance at a high-growth tech company

     

  • At least 2+ years in leadership roles, with a proven ability to hire, manage, and develop high-performing teams

     

  • Passion for building and leading a world-class finance function at a high-growth technology business

     

  • Degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, or Business Administration preferred; MBA a plus

     

  • Expert-level financial modeling skills and a strong grasp of GAAP financial statements

     

  • Outstanding analytical, problem-solving, and executive communication skills

     

  • Demonstrated success influencing executive teams and investors through data-driven insights

     

  • Ability to thrive in fast-paced, high-growth environments; startup experience strongly preferred

Application Instructions

If you’re interested in joining TRM, we encourage you to apply directly. Every application is reviewed by our Talent team.

Before applying, review the job description carefully and highlight the experience and impact that best demonstrate the required qualifications. Please also provide thoughtful and accurate answers to the application questions, as these will be used to evaluate your qualifications for the role.

If you send your resume directly to someone at TRM, we can’t guarantee it will reach the appropriate hiring team. Applying directly is the best way to ensure you’re considered.

What to Expect From Our Interview Process

Our process is designed to understand how you think, solve problems, and deliver impact, while giving you the opportunity to evaluate TRM. Most interview processes include a case study, AI skills assessment, and Leadership Principles interview.

  • Recruiter Intro: Explore your experience, motivations, and alignment with the role.

  • Hiring Manager: Dive deeper into your relevant experience, skills, and impact.

  • First Round: Typically 1–2 interviews focused on the skills most critical to the role.

  • Final Round: Typically 3–5 interviews to go deeper on your craft, problem-solving, and alignment with TRM.

  • References: We’ll speak with former colleagues who can provide perspective on your work and impact.

  • Offer: If it’s a mutual fit, your recruiter will walk you through your offer and answer your questions.

  • Welcome to TRM: Once you sign, we’ll get you ready for your first day and onboarding.

Your recruiter will share your specific interview plan and preparation guidance along the way.

Learn more about interviewing at TRM

Life at TRM

We are building a safer world. That promise shows up in how we work every day.

TRM moves quickly. We are a high velocity, high ownership team that expects clarity, follow-through, and impact. People who thrive here are energized by hard problems, experimentation, and continuous feedback. If something takes months elsewhere, it will ship here in days.

Our work sits at the intersection of AI, national security, and fighting crime. The problems are complex, the stakes are real, and the environment evolves quickly. The pace and intensity of the work reflect the importance of the mission. As a result, the way we operate requires a high level of ownership, adaptability, collaboration, and creative problem-solving.

At TRM, you should expect:

  • Priorities and targets to change quickly as we experiment and iterate

  • Work that often requires operating with a high degree of ambiguity

  • A high level of personal ownership and accountability

  • Close collaboration across teams and functions

  • Frequent, high-touch communication

  • Creative problem solving and out-of-the-box thinking

  • A pace that rewards urgency, adaptability, and outcomes

This environment is energizing for people who enjoy building, solving hard problems, and making progress in situations that are not always fully defined. It also requires comfort navigating ambiguity, adjusting course as new information emerges, and maintaining focus and positivity in a fast-moving and intense environment.

We also recognize that this style of operating is not for everyone. If you are primarily optimizing for predictability or a consistently balanced workload, we encourage you to use the interview process to pressure test whether this environment is truly the right fit. We want teammates who thrive here, not just survive here.

At the same time, many people find this work deeply rewarding. If you are excited by meaningful problems, motivated by ambitious goals, and energized by working alongside mission-driven colleagues, there is a good chance you will find TRM to be an exceptional place to grow and contribute. Learn more: Interviewing at TRM: How We Hire and What Success Looks Like

We enable individuals to express views on real-world events by trading on outcomes across politics, economics, sports, culture, and current affairs. Built as a peer-to-peer marketplace with no centralized "house," Polymarket aggregates diverse opinions into transparent, market-based probabilities that reflect collective expectations about the future.

We're growing fast, both in terms of volume ($21B traded in 2025) and adoption as an alternative news source. Our ambition is to become a ubiquitous beacon of truth in global media and we need your help adding fuel to the fire.

Sports is one of Polymarket's biggest growth vectors. We have active league partnerships and a product that maps naturally onto the sports betting and fan engagement space. What we don't yet have is someone who owns the creative layer of that entirely. This role exists to fix that.

You'll sit within the Design team as a senior individual contributor, working directly with partnership, marketing, and product leads. The mandate is straightforward: build the creative systems that let us activate against marquee sports moments fast, look legitimate doing it, and stay on the right side of league compliance. That means co-branded campaign work, in-app design, paid social, CTV, experiential, and everything in between.

  • Lead creative across all sports and league partnership activations, including co-branded campaigns, in-app integrations, paid social, display, CTV, and event assets.
